extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies, regulated entities, legal counsel, potential defendants, and other stakeholders subject to the Administrative False Claims Act (AFCA) and FLRA procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural regulations the Federal Labor Relations Authority proposes to implement the Administrative False Claims Act (AFCA), detailing investigation, complaint, hearing, post-hearing, appeal, and penalty-assessment processes for alleged false claims or statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Inflation Adjustment of Penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjustment of the statutory civil penalty amount from $5,000 to $12,500 pursuant to the 2015 Inflation Adjustment Act cap of 150 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains calculation: 150% of $5,000 is $7,500; add to base to yield $12,500. Notes this is less than a full CPI comparison and invites public comment on adjustment methodology and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory scope and liability (legal authority)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart implements the Administrative False Claims Act, codified at 31 U.S.C. 3801 through 3812. Liability for false claims can include an assessment of up to twice the amount of the false claim and a civil penalty. The civil penalty for a false claim or false statement actionable under that section is $12,500.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites authority sections and notes the subpart's intent to cite controlling statute where possible and repeat only where convenient to regulated public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations — Timeframes for notice and actions
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice to a person alleged to be liable must be mailed or delivered by the timeframes in 31 U.S.C. 3808(a): the later of 6 years after violation or 3 years after facts were known/should have been known, but in no event more than 10 years after the violation. A civil action to recover a penalty or assessment must be commenced within the 3-year timeframe noted in 31 U.S.C. 3808(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes statute-based limitations periods governing when notice and civil actions may be brought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time
rubrics_metrics.description: In computing any period under this part, time begins the day after the act, includes the last day unless that day is a weekend or federal holiday, and then includes the next business day. When allowed period is less than 7 days, intermediate weekends/holidays are excluded. If served by mail, add 5 days to response time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific rules for calculating deadlines and accommodating weekends/holidays and mailed service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stays ordered by the Department of Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Attorney General or designated Assistant Attorney General transmits a written finding that continuation of the administrative process may adversely affect any pending or potential criminal or civil action, the authority head shall stay the process immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authority head may resume only upon written authorization of DOJ official; protects DOJ criminal/civil prosecutions from interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional referrals for related misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal agencies that receive or discover specific information regarding bribery, gratuities, conflict of interest, or other corruption related to a false claim or statement must immediately report that information consistent with 31 U.S.C. 3808(c) to the Attorney General and agency Inspector General as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandates reporting of related corrupt activity uncovered in AFCA investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of contract appeals — procedural precedence
rubrics_metrics.description: If an agency uses a presiding officer who is a member of a board of contract appeals, the procedural rules implemented by that board will control to the extent there is inconsistency between the board's procedural rules and the procedural rules of this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which procedural set governs when a board of contract appeals presiding officer is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigating official authority and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The investigating official may investigate using subpoena authority at 31 U.S.C. 3804 or other authority (e.g., Inspector General Act). If investigation indicates AFCA action may be warranted, the investigating official shall submit a report of findings and conclusions to the reviewing official. May refer allegations directly to DOJ or defer referrals to avoid interference with criminal investigations; must report criminal law violations to the Attorney General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains investigative tools, reporting duty to reviewing official, and discretion to refer or defer for DOJ prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing official determination and written notice content
rubrics_metrics.description: If the reviewing official determines there is adequate evidence to believe a person is liable under AFCA and a reasonable prospect of collecting, the reviewing official shall transmit to the Attorney General written notice of intent to have a complaint issued. The written notice must include: (i) reasons for issuing a complaint; (ii) evidence supporting allegations; (iii) description of claims/statements forming basis; (iv) estimate of amount requested or demanded in violation; (v) statement of any exculpatory/mitigating circumstances known; and (vi) statement that there is a reasonable prospect of collecting appropriate penalties and assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets mandatory content for the reviewing official's written notice to DOJ, ensuring transparency of the basis for referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for authorization from the Department of Justice and $1,000,000 cap rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint may be issued only if DOJ approves issuance in writing and, for allegations under 31 U.S.C. 3802(a)(1) with respect to a claim, the reviewing official determines that the amount demanded in violation for such claim or a related group of claims submitted at the same time does not exceed $1,000,000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'related group of claims submitted at the same time' as claims arising from the same transaction submitted simultaneously; also clarifies this section does not limit authority to join unrelated claims in a single complaint regardless of amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written notifications per statute
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing official shall make all appropriate written notifications required by section 3803(j)(2) of title 31, U.S. Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms statutory notification obligations to affected parties as part of pre-complaint procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The complaint must identify: (1) allegations of liability including statutory basis, identification of claims/statements and reasons why liability arises; (2) the maximum amount of penalties and assessments; (3) instructions for filing an answer including right to request a hearing and representation; (4) identification/contact for government employee representing reviewing official if not handled personally; (5) fact that failure to file answer within 30 days will result in imposition of maximum penalties and assessments without right to appeal; and (6) at service, the defendant must be served with a copy of these regulations or be identified a free online resource where they can access them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies precise information the complaint must convey to ensure defendant awareness of allegations, rights, and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service timing of the complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: The Federal Labor Relations Authority must mail or deliver the complaint in accordance with 31 U.S.C. 3803(d)(1) within the time limitations identified at 31 U.S.C. 3808(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ties service timing to statutory limitations to ensure timely notice consistent with AFCA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer requirements and 30-day filing period
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant may file an answer within 30 days of service by mail or facsimile. In the answer, defendant shall: (i) admit or deny each allegation; (ii) state any defense intended to rely on; (iii) may state reasons penalties should be less than statutory maximum; and (iv) state name, postal address, email address, phone number of person authorized to act as defendant's representative, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes content of responsive pleading and contact information to facilitate proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to request a hearing and general answer/extension procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant may request a hearing with the presiding officer within 30 days of service. If unable to file an answer meeting requirements, the defendant may file a general answer denying liability and requesting a hearing and an extension to file a full answer; the presiding officer may grant up to 30 additional days for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows defendants a limited procedural safety valve to request hearing and seek extension for detailed answers; presiding officer decides expeditiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default upon failure to file an answer
rubrics_metrics.description: If defendant does not file an answer within prescribed time, reviewing official must refer complaint to presiding officer. Upon referral, presiding officer shall serve notice that an initial decision will be issued, assume facts alleged are true, and if facts establish liability, issue initial decision imposing maximum penalties and assessments. Failure to timely answer generally waives right to further review; initial decision becomes final 30 days after issuance unless stayed by timely appeal or motion to reopen for extraordinary circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes consequences of non-response, procedures for motions to reopen for extraordinary circumstances, and appeal rights limited to authority head on motion denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presiding officer disqualification — motion and affidavit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A presiding officer may be removed on initiative or motion by parties for disqualification. The motion must be accompanied by an affidavit alleging personal bias or other reason, filed promptly upon discovery, stating specific facts and time/circumstances of discovery, and accompanied by a certificate of representative of record that it is made in good faith. Upon filing the presiding officer shall proceed no further until the matter is resolved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets strict informational and timeliness requirements for disqualification motions to prevent undue delay and ensure good-faith assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority of the presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer shall conduct a fair and impartial hearing, avoid delay, maintain order, and assure record. Authority includes: (i) set/change hearing date/time/place; (ii) continue/recess hearing; (iii) hold conferences to identify/simplify issues; (iv) administer oaths; (v) issue subpoenas for attendance/testimony and production per 31 U.S.C. 3804(b)(2); (vi) rule on motions and procedural matters; (vii) regulate motion requirements and response times; (viii) regulate scope/timing of discovery; (ix) regulate course of hearing and conduct of parties, including imposing sanctions reasonably related to failure/misconduct; (x) examine witnesses; (xi) receive/rule on/exclude/limit evidence; (xii) take official notice of facts on motion; (xiii) decide cases or parts by summary judgment where no disputed material fact; (xiv) conduct conferences/arguments/hearings in person or by telephone/videoconference; (xv) exercise other necessary authority; (xvi) not have authority to find Federal statutes or regulations invalid; (xvii) not consult a person on a fact in issue except as authorized and not be supervised by investigating or reviewing official except as authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive list of presiding officer powers and express limits to preserve impartial adjudication and separation from investigative/reviewing officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing entitlement to review and obtain information
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendants receiving notice of hearing are entitled to information identified in 31 U.S.C. 3803(e), including copy of all relevant and material documents, transcripts, records, and other materials related to the allegations and upon which findings and conclusions are based. Defendants should request such information from Government point of contact identified in complaint; information subject to payment of reasonable duplication fee will be provided expeditiously upon payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guarantees access to government-held evidence forming basis of allegations, subject to applicable fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery — availability, types, and standards for granting
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless mutually agreed, discovery is available only as ordered by presiding officer. Types of discovery that may be ordered: (A) requests for production of documents; (B) requests for admissions; (C) written interrogatories; (D) depositions. A motion for discovery must be filed with requested discovery or depositions scope; opposition or protective order motion may be filed within 10 days. The presiding officer may grant discovery only if it finds the discovery sought: (A) is necessary for expeditious, fair, and reasonable consideration of issues; (B) is not unduly costly or burdensome; (C) will not unduly delay the proceeding; and (D) does not seek privileged information. The burden is on the party seeking discovery; the presiding officer shall regulate timing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes restrictive and case-specific discovery regime balancing fairness and expedition, with the moving party bearing burden of justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protective orders
rubrics_metrics.description: A party or prospective witness may file a motion for a protective order seeking to limit availability or disclosure of evidence. The presiding officer may issue orders to protect from annoyance, embarrassment, oppression, or undue burden/expense, including: (i) that discovery not be had; (ii) discovery only on specified terms/conditions; (iii) discovery through alternate methods; (iv) limit scope of inquiry; (v) conduct discovery with limited presence; (vi) seal contents of discovery/evidence; (vii) open sealed deposition only by order; (viii) protect trade secrets or confidential commercial information or criminal investigation materials; (ix) require simultaneous filing of specified documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanisms to protect confidentiality, trade secrets, and sensitive investigatory materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing orders — scheduling and minimum contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer shall issue scheduling orders appropriate to ensure a fair and impartial hearing, avoid delay, maintain order, and assure a record. At minimum the order must: (i) set hearing in permissible location under 31 U.S.C. 3803(g)(4); (ii) provide written notice required by 31 U.S.C. 3803(g)(2)(A); (iii) govern exchange of witness lists, statements, and exhibits; (iv) ensure defendant opportunity to present case, submit rebuttal evidence, and conduct cross-examination necessary for full disclosure of facts; and (v) include in any written notice a description of procedures for conduct of the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies minimum scheduling and disclosure protections to structure a fair hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing standard of proof
rubrics_metrics.description: The presiding officer will conduct the hearing consistent with authority to make determinations identified in 31 U.S.C. 3803(f) by a preponderance of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirms the preponderance standard for liability determinations in AFCA administrative hearings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining amount of penalties and assessments — enumerated factors
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining appropriate civil penalties and assessments, presiding officer and authority head should evaluate mitigating and aggravating circumstances and articulate reasons supporting penalties. The following, although not exhaustive, are factors that may influence determination: (1) number of false, fictitious or fraudulent claims or statements; (2) time period over which such claims/statements were made; (3) degree of defendant's culpability; (4) amount of money or value falsely claimed; (5) cost of Government's actual loss including foreseeable consequential damages and investigation costs; (6) relationship of civil penalty to Government's loss; (7) potential/actual impact on public confidence in management of Government programs; (8) whether defendant engaged in a pattern of similar misconduct; (9) whether defendant attempted to conceal misconduct; (10) degree to which defendant involved others in misconduct or concealing it; (11) where employee/agent misconduct is imputed, extent to which defendant's practices fostered or attempted to preclude such misconduct; (12) whether defendant cooperated in or obstructed investigation; (13) whether defendant assisted in identifying and prosecuting other wrongdoers; (14) complexity of program/transaction and defendant's sophistication/prior participation; (15) whether defendant has been found in other proceedings to have engaged in similar misconduct or dealt dishonestly with Government; (16) need to deter the defendant and others; (17) potential impact on rights of others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a detailed (17-item) non-exhaustive list of aggravating/mitigating factors to be considered and requires articulation of reasons underlying penalty amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of other factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this section limits the presiding officer or authority head from considering any other factors that in a given case may mitigate or aggravate the offense for which penalties and assessments are imposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves discretion to consider circumstances beyond the enumerated list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record — transcripts, availability, and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: The hearing shall be recorded and transcribed. Transcripts shall be available after the hearing at a cost not to exceed actual duplication cost and any court reporter's reasonable fee. The transcript of testimony, exhibits and other evidence admitted, and all filed documents constitute the record for decision. The record may be inspected and copied by anyone upon payment of a reasonable fee unless ordered otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets record-keeping and public-access rules and cost-recovery for transcripts/records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-hearing motions and briefs — timing and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Presiding officer may decide post-hearing motions. Any party may file a post-hearing brief; the presiding officer shall fix time for filing such briefs not to exceed 60 days from date parties receive the transcript or stipulated record. Briefs may be accompanied by proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law; presiding officer may permit reply briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes a 60-day maximum for filing post-hearing briefs and allows proposed findings and replies at presiding officer's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for good cause, the presiding officer shall issue a written decision required by 31 U.S.C. 3803(h) within 90 days after the time for submission of post-hearing briefs and reply briefs, if permitted, has expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a 90-day target for issuance of written initial decisions following briefing to promote timely resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to the authority head — procedures and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may not appeal interlocutory rulings. Except in default cases, if defendant is determined liable the defendant may appeal decision to the authority head by filing notice of appeal accompanied by a written brief specifying exceptions and reasons. Notice of appeal may be filed within 30 days after presiding officer issues decision; authority head may extend initial 30-day period for additional 30 days for good cause upon timely request. The reviewing official's representative may file opposition within 30 days of receiving the appeal. Authority head's review occurs within limitations noted in 31 U.S.C. 3803(i)(2)(B) and (C). There is no right to appear personally before the authority head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies appellate timing, brief content, extension procedures, opposition filing, statutory scope limitations, and no in-person appearance right before authority head.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3805 of title 31, U.S. Code, authorizes judicial review by an appropriate United States District Court of a final decision of the authority head imposing penalties and/or assessments under this part and specifies procedures for such review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies statutory authorization and channel for district court review of final administrative AFCA decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection of penalties and assessments
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections 3806 and 3808(b) of title 31, U.S. Code, authorize actions for collection of civil penalties and assessments imposed under this part and specify procedures for such actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directs to statutory collection mechanisms and procedures following final administrative or judicial judgments.
